judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear exclusion of litigation costs with a single named carve-back; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-back points to Subsection 22, which exists and matches, so the cross-reference holds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extracted text mislabels the paragraph '(i)' where the body twice refers to 'Exclusion 12(j)' — a mechanical inconsistency, though the carve-backs themselves are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The lettering slip also matters because Exclusion 12(i) genuinely exists and covers legal fees, so a reader tracing references could be misled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'knowingly having given or surrendered' in 'any exchange or purchase' is broad and the knowledge element is fact-sensitive; the carve-backs are precise, however.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves Insuring Clause 7 and Property losses under Insuring Clause 5 but not Money losses under Clause 5, which bears directly on fraudulently induced transfers under the Computer Fraud definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line exclusion whose key phrase 'to the advantage of any other Insured' is undefined and could be read narrowly (intra-group transfers) or broadly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Insured includes every Organization designated in Item 4 (the parent 'and its subsidiaries') plus ERISA and Non-ERISA Plans, this exclusion could bite on ordinary intercompany losses, a tension with the Non-Accumulation provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'similar recognized place of safe deposit' and 'any person who is duly authorized ... to have custody' are broad catch-alls following specific institutions, and the proviso converts the exclusion into excess coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the Other Insurance provision in Subsection 30 and the In Transit definition, which also contemplates authorised custodians — a reader must reconcile the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any authorized representative of an Insured' is undefined and potentially very wide, and it is chained to a list closed by 'or other fraudulent, dishonest or criminal act' — a double catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read broadly it could swallow Insuring Clauses 4 through 8, since employees and officers are all authorised representatives in some sense, which sits uneasily with the Third Party definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subparagraph (a) enumerates 'agent, broker, factor, commission merchant, consignee, contractor, independent contractor, subcontractor or other similar representative' — a textbook ejusdem generis catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against the Employee definition, which expressly includes leased and temporary personnel and volunteers, so the two must be reconciled to know who is covered under Insuring Clause 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two concrete carve-outs by named defined terms and by mail/carrier status; little interpretive room.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the separation between Insuring Clauses 2 and 3 and the electronic-fraud clauses, consistently with the Insuring Clause 5 and 6 grants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'kidnap, ransom or other extortion payment (as distinct from Robbery)' draws a line explicitly, but 'other extortion payment ... surrendered ... as a result of a threat' remains a general term after two specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Coverage Summary includes a Special Coverage (Kidnap/Ransom & Extortion) section whose forms are scheduled but whose text is not in this document, so the interface between the two sections cannot be checked from the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Confined to registered or coupon obligations and coupons, described with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It narrows Insuring Clause 4 only, and the Financial Instrument definition does not obviously reach such obligations anyway, making it belt-and-braces.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'becomes aware of a Computer Fraud or other fraudulent, dishonest or criminal act' uses an awareness trigger untethered to the defined Discovery term, and closes a list with a broad catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Crime Endorsement No. 4 deletes Exclusion 17 in its entirety, so this printed exclusion is not operative — a direct conflict visible only by reading the endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion of loss caused by 'any forgery or alteration of, on or in any written instrument' uses lower-case 'forgery' where the section defines 'Forgery', and it nearly negates the coverage grant it qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Credit Card Fraud is itself defined as the Forgery or alteration of a written instrument, so Exclusion 18 excludes precisely what Insuring Clause 8 insures unless the two conditions are met — a near-circular relationship.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three overlapping limbs ((a), (b) and (c) largely repeat one another) with a sixty-day post-termination discovery-and-notice window; the repetition is redundant but not obscure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3 amends Exclusion 19 'in its entirety' to delete the sixty-day window, while Endorsement No. 5 separately amends Exclusion 19 'in its entirety' to keep it — two endorsements to the same policy give irreconcilable versions of this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'owned by ... or for which the Organization is legally liable, or held ... in any capacity whether or not the Organization is liable' is layered but each limb is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates the Insuring Clause 1 and Clause 9 treatment of Client property and the Premises damage limit, matching the Client definition without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical amendment provision; its terms (payment held for the plan's benefit, substituted words, no retention) are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (b) deletes 'sixty (60) days' from Exclusion 19 and substitutes one year, but Endorsement No. 3 rewrites Exclusion 19 so that no such words exist, leaving the amendment inoperable on that version.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable court costs and attorneys' fees' with a prior-consent condition; a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly preserved by the carve-back in Exclusion 12(i) and its two-year suit limitation appears in Subsection 27(b), so the cross-references line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but highly specified: a ten-percent revenue test, a sixty-day notice deadline and an express null-and-void consequence; 'in its sole discretion' is broad but plainly allocated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3(2) rewrites the first paragraph of Subsection 23 to limit new-subsidiary coverage to loss Discovered after the acquisition, so the printed first paragraph here is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four cumulative conditions plus a limits rule, each drafted concretely; 'some or all of the coverage' is slightly loose but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3(3) deletes Subsection 24 in its entirety and deletes all references to it, so this entire printed provision is inoperative while Subsection 25 still opens with 'Subject to Subsection 24'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extremely long but mechanical: each lettered limb states a single-limit aggregation rule keyed to a Declarations item, with 'series of related acts' the only elastic phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its opening words 'Subject to Subsection 24' point to a provision Endorsement 3 deleted, and Endorsement 3(4) replaces its first paragraph with a discovery-based trigger that conflicts with the sustained-during-the-Policy-Period language printed here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two crisp non-accumulation rules; 'shall not be cumulative from year to year' is standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Subsection 25's single-limit rules and with Exclusion 19's bar on double recovery under renewals, and with the deleted Subsection 24 its prior-policy reference loses some of its object.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete deadlines (ninety days, six months, two years) and enumerated duties; the inventory-comparison sentence is convoluted but its rule is discernible, and the (a)/(b) sub-lettering is displaced in the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The ninety-day condition precedent sits against Endorsement/Rider No. 1's prejudice requirement and General Terms Subsection 5's excuse for late notice, and the two-year suit bar must be read with Subsection 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A least-of valuation formula with named published sources and fixed measuring dates; 'Lost Instrument Bond' is undefined but is a term of art.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes General Terms Subsection 6 for this coverage section, which that provision expressly permits, so the overlap is anticipated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-step waterfall stated in order, with 'less the cost of recovery' defined by position; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the subrogation clause in General Terms Subsection 7 and the excess structure of Other Insurance in Subsection 30.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'null and void to the extent of the amount recoverable or received' is awkward — 'recoverable' and 'received' are different tests — and 'any other party in interest' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 12(m) already makes this coverage excess over custodial insurance, so the two excess mechanisms overlap and could be read to double-count.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-word amendment adding 'trustee' to the list of Executives; entirely mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cleanly replaces subparagraph (a) of the printed Executive definition, and no other endorsement touches that term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate on headings and unchanged terms; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'all other terms remain unchanged' formula becomes strained where later endorsements amend the same clause, but this endorsement does not overlap with any other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare deletion instruction, unambiguous in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes Exclusion 12(b) while substituting broader privacy exclusions in the same endorsement, so the printed Exclusion 12(b) in the coverage section is superseded — a conflict apparent only across documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Each limb closes with 'or any similar type of nonpublic information' after a long enumerated list, and 'loss involving' is a notably loose causal link — a general-versus-specific and vagueness problem together.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-back preserves only Insuring Clause 6, so a loss flowing from a spoofed email under Insuring Clause 5 could be argued to be excluded as 'involving' misused information — squarely engaging the computer-fraud grants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate about headings and unchanged terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the identical clauses in the other endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extracted text carries orphan numerals and a stray full stop ('for.'), but the substituted rule — loss must be sustained and Discovered before termination — is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 5 also amends Exclusion 19 'in its entirety' to a materially different text that allows sixty days after termination, so two endorsements to the same policy give conflicting versions of the same exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical substitution of the first paragraph of Subsection 23; the substituted words are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It changes new-subsidiary coverage from an acquisition-date trigger to a discovery trigger while the remaining paragraphs of Subsection 23 (notice, additional premium, null-and-void) stay as printed, so the amended provision must be read against unamended text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blanket deletion including 'any and all references to Subsection 24', stated plainly though without listing them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection 25 opens 'Subject to Subsection 24 Liability for Prior Losses' and Subsection 26 refers to prior bonds, so the sweep of this deletion across the section is something a reader must work out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single substituted sentence with two clear conditions — sustained prior to termination and Discovered during the Policy Period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with Endorsement No. 5's version of Exclusion 19, which allows discovery and notice within sixty days after termination, and with the printed Subsection 25 requiring loss 'sustained ... during the Policy Period'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate headings and unchanged-terms language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Here the 'all other terms remain unchanged' formula is strained, because Endorsement No. 5 later purports to rewrite the very exclusion this endorsement rewrote.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare deletion of a numbered exclusion; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 17 remains printed in the coverage section text, so the instrument as delivered contains an exclusion that this endorsement removes — resolvable but a cross-document conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate on headings and unchanged terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other endorsement addresses Exclusion 17, so the unchanged-terms formula creates no difficulty here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Restates Exclusion 19 with three overlapping limbs and adds 'issued by the Company or by any affiliate of the Company' to the renewal proviso; repetitive but each limb is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3 already amended Exclusion 19 'in its entirety' to delete the sixty-day window, and this endorsement restores it, so the policy carries two irreconcilable versions of the same exclusion and of the Subsection 25 trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate on headings and unchanged terms, with page furniture embedded in the extract.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'all other terms remain unchanged' statement is difficult to apply given that Endorsement No. 3 had already rewritten the same exclusion, which is exactly the point of friction.
